# Exact section-preserving support bumps for uniform convex bodies

This is an all-dimensional physical variation lemma for UNIFORM convex
bodies. It preserves every chosen central section as an ACTUAL SET,
not merely its centroid to first order. It gives an exact finite cap
ratio identity and excludes smooth positive-curvature local minima of
the weighted stationary-menu functional, except the classwise antipodal
case whose value is exactly 1/2.

For a full minimal circuit of equal ACTUAL deepest caps, a separate
parallel-cover argument also gives actual ordinary-depth descent. Without
that extra maximal-depth hypothesis, only the stationary-menu objective
is decreased. No reduction of nonsmooth minimizers to simplices or full
weighted stationary-section theorem is asserted.

## 1. The ordinary uniform geometry and objective

Let d>=2, K subset R^d be a positive convex body with 0 in int K. Fix
finitely many unit continuous normals u_i and positive weights theta_i,
sum theta_i=1. Let

    H_i={X:u_i.X>=0},
    Q_i=|K intersect H_i|,
    S_i=H^(d-1)(K intersect u_i-perp),
    Phi(K)=sum_i theta_i Q_i/|K|.                         (1)

Assume the actual section centroids equal zero and

    sum_i theta_i S_i u_i=0.                             (2)

These are the weighted stationary-section hypotheses. They do not say
the Q_i are equal or that zero is deepest in K. The construction below
keeps every section, normal and theta_i fixed, and hence preserves (2)
and all the section-centroid equations exactly.

In the basic theorem assume K is C^2 with everywhere positive Gaussian
curvature. Equivalently its support function h on the unit sphere is
C^2, positive, and

    A_h(n)=Hess_S h(n)+h(n) I

is positive definite on every spherical tangent space. Its inverse
Gauss parametrization is X(n)=h(n)n+grad_S h(n). Section 2a proves a
local version: this positive-definite support description is needed only
near the chosen normal patch, and the rest of K may be nonsmooth.

## 2. An actual two-sided deformation with fixed section traces

Choose an open normal patch U whose closure maps by X into one STRICT
cap-signature cone

    Omega={X:sign(u_i.X)=s_i for every i},  s_i in {-,+}.

Shrink U so every |u_i.X(n)| on its closure is bounded below by a
positive number. Choose a nonzero smooth function psi>=0 with compact
support in U, and set

    h_t=h+t psi.                                         (3)

For every sufficiently small SIGNED t, h_t stays positive and
A_(h_t)=A_h+t A_psi stays positive definite. Thus it is the support
function of an actual C^2 positive-curvature convex body K_t with
0 in its interior. Both inward and outward variations are available;
this is not a claim about arbitrary signed facet velocities.

The perturbed boundary parametrization is EXACTLY

    X_t(n)=X(n)+t[psi(n)n+grad_S psi(n)].                 (4)

Outside the support of psi it equals X(n). On that support it remains
inside Omega for small |t|. Consequently every radial direction outside
Omega is unchanged. Indeed its old boundary point is outside Omega,
so its old supporting normal is outside the bump patch; equation (4)
leaves that same point on boundary K_t. A convex body containing zero
has only one boundary point on each ray. Thus its radial endpoint is
unchanged. Equivalently, every changed radial shell lies in Omega.

Each cutting plane u_i-perp has all its nonzero radial directions
outside Omega. It follows that

    K_t intersect u_i-perp=K intersect u_i-perp
       for EVERY i and all sufficiently small signed t.   (5)

This is an exact set identity. It preserves section areas, first moments,
centroids, the original normal rank, and every original balanced circuit.
No threshold reoptimization or Schur complement is needed to establish
this constrained stationary variation.

If t>0 then h_t>=h and K_t strictly contains K; if t<0 it is strictly
contained in K. Hence Delta V(t)=|K_t|-|K| has the sign of t. Its usual
actual first variation is

    V'(0)=integral_(boundary K) psi(n_X) dH^(d-1)(X)>0.   (6)

It may also be obtained directly from the radial derivative
rho'(omega)=psi(n)/(n.omega), with the positive denominator bounded away
from zero. The construction itself and the finite identity below do
not rely on neglecting a remainder in (6).

### 2a. The same exact variation in a smooth Gauss patch of a nonsmooth body

For an individual bump, assume only that the support function of K is
C^2 with positive-definite A_h on an open neighborhood of the compact
support of psi. Assume the corresponding boundary points have the strict
signature and positive margins used above. Elsewhere K is an arbitrary
positive convex body. Then (3)--(7) remain valid.

Here is the global convexity justification. The positively homogeneous
extension of h_t is locally convex away from zero: in a neighborhood of
the bump support this follows from positive-definite A_(h_t), and off
that neighborhood it is the unchanged support function. Its restriction
to any line avoiding zero is locally convex, hence convex. On a line
through zero it has two linear pieces with nondecreasing slopes, because
h_t(n)+h_t(-n)>0. Thus the extension is globally convex and homogeneous,
and h_t is an actual support function. Positivity also keeps zero inside
K_t. No gluing of merely formal normal velocities is used.

It remains to justify fixed radial endpoints when the old boundary is
nonsmooth. If an old boundary point p is outside Omega, none of its
supporting normals can lie in the bump support: every such normal has
the unique support point X(n) inside Omega. Choose a supporting normal
of p outside that support. The old and new homogeneous support functions
agree on a neighborhood of this normal. Their convex subdifferentials,
and hence their support faces there, agree. In particular p remains on
boundary K_t, for both signs of t. The radial uniqueness argument giving
(5) is therefore unchanged. Formula (6) involves only the smooth bump
patch and can equivalently be obtained there by radial integration.

Consequently every admissible positive-curvature normal patch avoiding
the cuts must have W=Phi at a local minimum of the fixed-section menu
functional. In particular, a positive-curvature patch that crosses just
one cutting-plane class with nonzero orientation imbalance is excluded:
its two sides have different W. This is a local obstruction even when
the rest of the body is polyhedral or otherwise nonsmooth. It does not
assert that an arbitrary nonsmooth minimizer has such a patch.

## 3. Exact cap response and finite normalized descent

Set e_i=1 if s_i=+ and e_i=0 otherwise, and put W=sum theta_i e_i.
All radial volume changes occur in Omega, where every cap indicator
is constant. Therefore

    |K_t intersect H_i|-Q_i=e_i Delta V(t),
    Phi(K_t)-Phi(K)=[W-Phi(K)] Delta V(t)/|K_t|.          (7)

These are exact finite equalities for both signs of t. They use uniform
volume on the actual changed body; no abstract cap-marginal density is
substituted.

If W<Phi, choose t>0; if W>Phi, choose t<0. In either case (7) gives
strict descent while retaining every stationary section as a set.
This is a shape deformation distinct from rotating an isolated critical
cap of a fixed body, which can be prohibited by its nondegenerate Hessian.

## 4. A nontrivial smooth stationary menu always has such a patch

Group normals having the same unoriented cutting plane. For each group
let theta_+ and theta_- be its total weights on the two orientations,
and let alpha=theta_+-theta_-. If EVERY group has alpha=0, its two
opposite cap masses sum to |K| and the total weighted mean is

    Phi(K)=1/2.                                         (8)

Otherwise choose a group with alpha nonzero. On its plane choose a
nonzero vector outside every other distinct cutting plane. A finite
union of proper linear subspaces cannot cover this plane, so this is
possible, including d=2. Its ray reaches a point p on boundary K which
is on the chosen cutting plane and no other one.

The chosen plane is transverse to boundary K at p: if its normal were
parallel to the outward normal of K there, it would be a supporting
plane through the interior point zero, impossible. Small boundary
patches on the two sides thus have signatures differing ONLY in that
group. Their W values differ by alpha and cannot both equal Phi(K).
The inverse Gauss map gives a normal patch of the type in Section 2 on
at least one of these sides. Equation (7) then gives strict descent.

Consequently a C^2 everywhere-positive-curvature body carrying a
stationary menu with a nonzero unoriented weight imbalance is NOT a
local minimizer of Phi among actual uniform bodies with those exact
section traces. In a full irreducible positive circuit (d>=2), opposite
normals cannot already form a proper balanced subcircuit, so the
classwise cancellation exception does not occur.

The conclusion is a genuine geometric exclusion, but only for the stated
smooth class. A Hausdorff approximation of a nonsmooth extremizer does
not preserve stationarity or local minimizing status, so it supplies no
unproved passage to a simplex or bounded-vertex stratum.

## 5. The additional hypotheses that turn this into deepest-point descent

Suppose now there are exactly d+1 normals forming a full minimal positive
circuit. In addition to the preceding hypotheses, assume

    Q_i=Q for all i,
    Q=max_(y in K) inf_(H contains y) |K intersect H|.     (9)

Thus the selected caps actually attain the global ordinary maximum at
the common source zero. Equal volumes at stationary sections alone would
not establish the second assertion of (9).

Apply a bump chosen by Section 4. Its changed radial shells stay a
positive distance from each original cutting plane, uniformly for small
t. Hence for small scalar thresholds b the cap function has the EXACT
form

    |K_t intersect {u_i.X>=b}|
       =|K intersect {u_i.X>=b}|+e_i Delta V(t).          (10)

The old cap function is C^1 at b=0 with derivative -S_i. Solve the
d+1 equations

    |K_t intersect {u_i.X>=u_i.y(t)}|=q(t),
    y(0)=0, q(0)=Q.                                     (11)

The Jacobian in (y,q) has rows (-S_i u_i,-1) and is invertible. Indeed
a vector in its kernel has u_i.v=-r/S_i; multiplying by theta_i S_i
and summing gives r=0 by (2), and spanning of the normals then gives
v=0. The ordinary implicit-function theorem supplies y(t),q(t).

Differentiating (11) and using (2) gives

    q'(0)=W V'(0),
    (q(t)/|K_t|)'_(t=0)=[W-Q/|K|] V'(0)/|K|.            (12)

For every t, the parallel caps in (11) cover ALL R^d: they pass through
y(t), and their fixed normals have the same positive dependence as
before. A point strictly outside every cap would contradict that
dependence. Consequently the new actual global ordinary maximum is at
most q(t), and its normalized value strictly decreases in the signed
direction chosen in Section 3.

The rebalanced caps in (11) need not themselves retain zero section
centroids. This is harmless for the global upper cover. The original
through-zero caps remain exactly stationary by (5). These are two
different valid uses of the same actual body path, not an assertion
that threshold reoptimization preserves section stationarity.

## 6. An exact disk calibration with an irreducible three-normal circuit

In d=2 start with the unit disk and the three unit normals at angles
0, 2pi/3, 4pi/3, with theta_i=1/3. All three central chords have length
2 and centroid zero, the normal circuit is irreducible and full rank,
and all cap areas are pi/2. The ordinary maximum is pi/2 at the origin.

In angular normal coordinates set

    psi(phi)=cos(6phi)^4 if |phi|<=pi/12, and 0 otherwise,
    h_t(phi)=1+t psi(phi),       0<t<=1/1000.             (13)

Psi is C^3 at the two joins. On its support, writing z=cos(6phi)^2,

    psi+psi''=432z-575z^2>=-143.

Thus h_t+h_t''>0 in the stated range. The old patch is in the signature
captured only by the first normal: its distance from either other cutting
line is at least sin(pi/12)>1/4. The boundary displacement in (4) is at
most |t|(|psi|+|psi'|)<=25|t|<=1/40, so the entire changed patch stays
strictly in that same signature. The exact fixed-section and cap identities
therefore apply without an unspecified sufficiently-small parameter.

The support-function area formula gives

    V_t=pi+pi t/16-2845pi t^2/1536,
    Delta V=pi t/16-2845pi t^2/1536>0.                   (14)

Indeed integral psi=pi/16, integral psi^2=35pi/768, and
integral (psi')^2=15pi/4. The three actual cap areas are

    pi/2+Delta V,       pi/2,       pi/2,

and the full-rank stationary weighted mean is exactly

    Phi(K_t)=1/2-Delta V/[6(pi+Delta V)]<1/2.             (15)

It remains safely above the desired lower bound in this small range.
The parallel equal-cover construction has normalized derivative -1/96
at t=0, supplying a concrete check of the distinct maximal-depth argument.
No exact formula for the entire later deepest-point path is inferred.

## 7. What remains unresolved

The lemma works in every continuous dimension and for genuine uniform
body geometry. It identifies actual two-sided variations preserving the
full section data and gives an exact objective formula. It does not
control facets or zero-curvature singular patches, and it does not show
that all relevant minima admit the required smooth patch.

For an arbitrary balanced stationary menu without (9), the conclusion
is only the finite weighted-menu descent (7). Neither global deepestness
nor a sharp Gamma_d lower bound is inferred from stationarity alone.
Mixed-fiber compatibility is not imposed here: propagating such a bump
through an actual mixed body is a separate physical problem.
